meta_description: Cyber resilience measured by rehearsal: immutable and isolated backups, restore drills that beat the signed RTO with headroom, and a console where the drill is the evidence of record.

blocks.x: Recovery that is rehearsed, not documented: immutable backups with integrity checks, clean-room restores that prove the RTO, and a command structure that has already survived its worst day — on a schedule, with evidence.
Your RTO is whatever your last rehearsal proved — nothing else
blocks.sub: Immutable vaults, clean rooms and timed drills as the only honest recovery story

blocks.x: Resilience is measured in one moment: the day ransomware lands, can you restore the business service faster than the signed RTO? Everything else — the runbooks, the immutability, the clean rooms — exists to make that answer yes without improvisation.

The practice covers immutable backup architecture, restore orchestration by business service (not by server), incident command that has been rehearsed, and the recovery evidence regulators and insurers ask for afterward.
Below: the failure modes that make recovery fictional, the reference architecture of rehearsed resilience, and the console that reports drill results as facts.

stages.name: Declare
stages.detail: Declaration criteria pre-agreed (encryption detected, domain admin compromise, exfil evidence); severity classes set the command structure — no debate at 3 a.m.

stages.name: Command
stages.detail: IC, forensic lead, recovery lead, comms lead, legal — each with a playbook; decisions priced in RTO/RPO arithmetic, not seniority.

stages.name: Contain
stages.detail: Containment prefers reversible actions (isolate, disable, revoke) with evidence preserved — wiping the forensic trail to stop the bleed is a priced decision.

stages.name: Restore
stages.detail: Recovery runs through the clean-room environment with per-tier order and integrity gates — ledger reconciliation before a service is declared restored.

stages.name: Learn
stages.detail: Review within two weeks with drill-grade findings; the resilience backlog absorbs them — repeat classes escalate to the board metric.

widgets.note: The playbook is rehearsed annually with executives in the room — crisis command is a rehearsed operation, not an org chart.

blocks.sub: Immutable vaults, clean-room restores and timed rehearsals — recovery as measured fact

blocks.x: Recovery plans are fictional until rehearsed: the runbook references a backup nobody tested, the vault shares identity with the domain the ransomware owns, and the RTO on the slide has never been measured. The discipline makes recovery a systems property — business services carry named RTO/RPO targets, snapshots are immutable and air-gapped, the vault sits on a separate identity plane (compromised domain credentials cannot reach it), and the clean-room restore rebuilds into a segregated network before anything touches production. Rehearsals are timed, per service tier, and the drill evidence — actual restore duration — is the only RTO anyone is allowed to state.

Incident command is trained like a fire drill: named roles, a communication plan with pre-drafted holding statements, and decision thresholds written while calm. The console reads drill results per business service; the review asks the hard question — which service's RTO slipped, and what changes before the next drill.

items: Recovery claims come from timed drills; slides do not count.
Immutable, air-gapped, unreachable by compromised domain credentials.
Rebuild segregated first; production touch is a decision, not a default.
Named roles and decision thresholds written while calm.
What does "your RTO is whatever your last rehearsal proved" mean?

Exactly that: an RTO written in a document is an aspiration. The signed RTO stands only while the last drill achieved it with headroom — the console shows signed versus drill-achieved per service, and a missed drill invalidates the claim.
How do backups survive a ransomware attack with domain admin?

Immutable, isolated: backup copies are immutable within a window and isolated from the production identity plane. The restore path assumes the attacker holds domain admin — which is the drill that matters.

Per the drill calendar: every business service drills against its signed RTO on a cadence, with scenarios rotated — partial corruption, region loss, identity-plane compromise — and results posted to the console.
What does incident command get at handover?
The drill calendar, the runbooks from real drills, the console and the gates — command shifts from improvising a recovery to executing the rehearsed one, with evidence the drill already produced.
Can you work with our existing backup estate?
Yes — the integration surface names the backup estates and business services. Where immutability or isolation is missing, the defaults table names the deviation and the price of signing it.
